verdict.rationale: Neon has a dedicated Scale to Zero doc and states that idle databases incur no ongoing compute overhead. A free tier with no time limit and no credit card covers prototypes, and separated storage and compute plus instant restore support data staying durable while compute is off. A community user calls pay-per-use pricing a game-changer for hobby projects, though others note that paid-tier minimums and storage costs apply beyond light use. Missing for 10: substantive scale-to-zero doc content (suspend timing, cold-start behavior), explicit durability guarantees while suspended, and recent hands-on corroboration that idle projects truly cost nothing.
